pll1d22c3-d1e3501.summary: Notes a name said of no person singly but of all together, 'Trinity,' which is not said by substance but, as a quasi-collective term, designates the plurality of persons.
claims: 'Trinity' is said only of all three together.
It designates plurality of persons, not substance.

pll1d22c3-d1e3504.summary: Notes names that befit God from time and are not relative, as 'incarnate,' 'made man.'
claims: Some temporal names are not relative.

pll1d22c3-d1e3507.summary: Concludes that six differences of names have been assigned, each of which must be treated.
claims: There are six kinds of divine names.

pl-l1d22c3.summary: Completes the classification. 'Trinity' is said of no person singly but of all together, not by substance but as a quasi-collective name of the plurality of persons. Some names befit God from time but are not relative, as 'incarnate' and 'made man.' So there are six differences among the names used of God, each to be treated.
claims: 'Trinity' is said only of all three persons together, as a quasi-collective name.
Some temporal names are not relative, as 'incarnate.'
There are six kinds of divine names.
